item.title: Poll: So, Are You Getting The Zelda Switch 2 Console And Pro Controller?
item.description:
Mipha-ntastic.

Just recently, a pretty seismic leak made its way across the internet, revealing the apparent existence of a new Zelda-themed Switch 2 console and accompanying Pro Controller.

Produced to celebrate the series' 40th anniversary, the hardware boasts a rather lovely custom theme that includes heavy use of the iconic Triforce along with a mix of black, green, and gold colours.

item.title: Bethesda Aware Of Feedback Asking For Additional Oblivion Remastered Patch
item.description:
The Switch 2 version could also benefit from some post-launch updates.

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered is now available on the Switch 2. While it's in a playable state, the game's performance and some other things could potentially benefit from a patch or two.

While there's no specific patch announcement for the Nintendo version (at least yet), Bethesda has today acknowledged feedback from Oblivion players in general, noting how it's looking to bring optimisations from the new Switch 2 version to other platforms in the future.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: THQ's Sacred 2 Remaster Is Finally Available For Switch, Includes All Expansions & Updates
item.description:
The "legendary action RPG" returns.

Last week at the THQ Nordic Showcase, it was revealed the remaster of the "legendary action RPG" Sacred 2 was finally coming to the Nintendo Switch.

In case you missed it, this fantasy title featuring upgraded visuals and smoother combat is now officially available on the eShop.

item.title: Bethesda Just Hosted A Live Playthrough Of The Elder Scrolls VI
item.description:
The Xbox boss gets a sneak peek of "********" behind closed doors.

Bethesda is celebrating the release of The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered on the Switch 2 this week, but in some surprising news, it's also found time to showcase The Elder Scrolls VI.

Yes, you read that correctly, this week it's actually done a "live playthrough" of the next major chapter in the fantasy role-playing series. This update on the long-awaited title, which got an announcement teaser in 2018, was shared by Xbox's new boss, Asha Sharma.

item.title: Stardew Valley - Switch 2 Edition Physical Release Announced, Pre-Orders Now Live
item.description:
Including the Switch game and upgrade pack.

The farming and life sim Stardew Valley got a Nintendo Switch 2 Edition last year (and earlier this year in Europe) and a physical edition has now been announced.

Fangamer will be distributing a standard edition of the title for $39, which includes an 18-page full colour illustrated instruction manual. This version includes the base game and upgrade pack and is loaded with Version 1.6, with free updates available as they're released.

item.title: The Lord Of The Rings: War In The North Shadow-Drops On Switch 1 & 2
item.description:
Looks like meat's back on the menu, boys!

The mad lads at Aspyr have announced and shadow-dropped The Lord of the Rings: War in the North - Legacy Edition on Switch 1 & 2, reviving a 2011 curio for modern consoles.

Boasting local co-op (not on Switch 1), 60fps gameplay (this too - sorry), a new auto-save feature, and numerous bug fixes, the Legacy Edition is available now at $19.99. Curiously, however, Aspyr has clarified that those on the EU eShop will have to wait until the 18th for the Switch 2 release.

item.title: Elden Ring For Switch 2 Is Looking Pretty Slick In New Story Trailer
item.description:
Not so tarnished, eh?

Bandai Namco had released a new story trailer for Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition ahead of its Switch 2 launch on 28th August 2026.

While we're well aware that publishers like to show off games in their very best light for trailers, there's no denying that it actually looks really nice. After reports of some performance issues during hands-on sessions, it seems FromSoftware has taken the time to make sure it looks and runs well on Nintendo's console.

item.title: Review: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered (Switch 2) - A Solid Update Of All-Time Classic RPG
item.description:
To Weynon Priory, then.

15 years after its release, Skyrim is now well established as a household name in open-world RPGs. It captured the zeitgeist in a way that few games ever have, and is so enduring that its many re-releases are subject to memes. Yet Skyrim is just one section of the great Tamriel continent, and during the seventh console generation, the series hit its stride with Oblivion, the fourth entry in the Elder Scrolls saga.

In place of wasteland tundra and skies filled with dragons, Cyrodiil offers sprawling countryside, shining imperial citadels, and burning portals into demonic realms. Oblivion Remastered gives the complete adventure a fresh lick of Unreal Engine 5 paint, offering a huge main quest alongside excellent expansions Knights Of The Nine and Shivering Isles.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Little Nightmares III Dev Announces Layoffs With Up To 75 Employees Affected
item.description:
Supermassive disappointment.

Supermassive Games, the developer behind the likes of Little Nightmares III, Until Dawn, and The Dark Pictures Anthology, has announced it is to be begin a "redundancy consultancy process".

This, according to the studio, will result in the loss of up to 75 employees, with Supermassive calling it a necessary step to ensure the "sustainability of the company".

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: UK Charts: Resident Evil Requiem Gobbles A Herb And Is Back On Top
item.description:
Graceful ascent.

The latest UK boxed charts data is in, and it's a fairly quiet week with no major new entries for the Switch 1 & 2. PS5 and PC got Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, which debuts at number 6, while Game Freak's Beast of Reincarnation launched on PS5, PC, and Xbox, landing at number 5.

Meanwhile, Capcom's Resident Evil Requiem saw a nice boost in sales to jump all the way up to number one, beating Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and Pokémon Pokopia. A quick search only reveals that outlets are selling Requiem at roughly £10 less than the RRP, but we're not seeing any major discounts that could explain the bump in sales.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Video: Final Fantasy Resonance Trailer Highlights Series Legend Cloud Strife
item.description:
"You're finished".

Following the announcement of Final Fantasy Resonance back in June, Square Enix has begun highlighting the game's 'Visions', which are characters that can fight alongside you during the journey. We already caught a glimpse of the Warrior of Light the other day, and now it's the turn of series legend Cloud Strife.

The trailer is a pretty short one and it's admittedly low on gameplay footage, but we can see Cloud unleashing his signature moves during battle, albeit with the rather lovely HD-2D visuals utilised to full effect.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Development On Final Fantasy 9 Remake Reportedly "No Longer Moving Forward"
item.description:
"it was very far along".

Despite Square Enix still in the trenches with development on Final Fantasy VII Revelation, rumours have persisted that a remake of Final Fantasy IX isn't too far behind.

Unfortunately, according to a comment from Alex Donaldson (Editor, RPG Site) over on Reset Era, development on the remake is "no longer moving forward". He says that the game would have been a single entry rather than split across multiple releases, and that development was "very far along".

item.title: Rumour: Hazelight's Award-Winning Co-Op Game Might Be Coming To Switch 2
item.description:
'It Takes Two' was released for Switch in 2022.

We've already had multiple Switch titles receive a Switch 2 makeover recently, and it looks like another one may have been discovered ahead of the official announcement.

As highlighted by Nintendo Everything, a document by Chinese games distributor Prowell Asia Holdings features an image of a Switch 2 version of Hazelight's award-winning co-op adventure, It Takes Two. According to the same listing, the EA-published title will apparently arrive mid-October, include English language support, and is getting a Game-Key Card release. It's also supposedly about 12.1GB in size.

item.title: Genki's New Controller Is Chunky, Boasts Haptic Feedback, And Its Own Screen
item.description:
Kickstarter live soon.

Accessory manufacture Genki is getting into the controller space with the Manta, a premium pad that contains its own 2.79-inch screen and operating system for intuitive customisation without the need for a separate companion phone or desktop app.

So you can switch profiles, remap buttons, tune controls, edit macros, manage connections, and more directly on the controller itself. You've also got haptic feedback, up to 8,000hz polling rate when wired (1,000 wireless) and, remarkably, a proper headphone jack. Unfortunately, however, it only features 3-axis gyro.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Random: Metroid Prime In 2D Is Now A Reality Thanks To New Fan Project
item.description:
Back to the Origins.

Before Metroid Prime launched in 2002, the series had been exclusively 2D since its inception in the '80s. Now, Nintendo is able to play in both 2D and 3D spaces, but what if you could 'demake' Prime to be more like the original 2D titles?

That's exactly what Lv.4 GAMES has done with its new fan project: Metroid Prime Origins. It's a completely fresh adaptation of Prime that morphs it into an NES-inspired 2D adventure, complete with original sprites, sounds effects, and music.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: A Decade Later, No Man's Sky Fans Have Explored Less Than 1% Of Its Planets
item.description:
Hello Games celebrates its 10th anniversary.

No Man's Sky, unbelievably, launched a decade ago on 9th August 2016. Though it was met with mixed reviews at the time, developer Hello Games persevered and produced over thirty major updates for the game, transforming it into an impressive experience that you can play on both Switch and Switch 2.

To celebrate the milestone, Hello Games' founder and managing director Sean Murray has provided an open letter to fans to thank them for the support over the years. In it, he confirmed that although "tens of millions" of travellers have embarked upon journeys across the galaxies, less than 1% of the available planets have been explored. Mad.

Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Feature: "It's Disingenuous To Call It A Remake" - Bethesda On Why Oblivion For Switch 2 Is A Remaster
item.description:
"the core bones are still the original game".

I don't know about you, but one of my favourite memories of the Switch was the debut announcement trailer. Not only did it effortlessly communicate what the console could do, but it showcased one of the biggest games of the previous decade running on a teeny, tiny handheld. On an aeroplane. With the controllers detached.

"Wait, this thing can run Skyrim?!"

item.title: Review: LEGO Party! Nintendo Switch 2 Edition (Switch 2) - Comes At The Party King And Doesn't Miss
item.description:
Lego another round.

Like a beastly kraken ensnaring a ship in its countless tentacles, it’s getting harder to find a portion of the gaming landscape that Lego hasn’t infiltrated. From action-adventure offerings like LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight to racing with LEGO 2K Drive and puzzle-platforming with LEGO Voyagers, the monolithic toy brick brand has demonstrated that it can be adapted to just about any genre out there — so perhaps it’s not too shocking that it would eventually try its hand at the multiplayer party game scene with the aptly-named LEGO Party.

Lego Party opts for a virtual board-game format, allowing up to four players to compete in minigames and take turns traversing a handful of perilous and prize-filled maps in hopes of collecting enough Golden Bricks to be crowned the victor. The game features a range of — okay, okay, I managed to get at least 100 words into this review without mentioning Mario Party. Surely that has to count for something, right?

Read the full article on nintendolife.com
